extracted.intended_audience: Early-career postdoctoral researchers applying for the Royal Society University Research Fellowship (URF) 2026 and host-organisation approvers (Heads of Department, research/finance officers, referees).
extracted.subtask_description: Scheme notes and application guidance for the Royal Society University Research Fellowship (URF) 2026 round, specifying eligibility, funding rules, application/formatting requirements, assessment criteria, review process, and host organisation commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant research experience window (3–8 years post-PhD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to early career post-doctoral researchers with between three and eight years of actual research experience since their PhD by the closing date of the round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual research experience is calculated from the date the degree was approved by the board of graduate studies. Part-time contracts are pro‑rated. Cases of exceptional talent with <3 years may be considered with a Head of Department support letter submitted at least 3 weeks before deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of career breaks and pro‑rata part-time time
rubrics_metrics.description: Time spent outside the research environment (parental leave, extended sick leave, caring responsibilities, non-research employment) will be considered when assessing research experience eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For maternity/paternity/shared parental/adoptive leave and extended sick leave (>4 weeks): in addition to actual time taken off, an additional amount equivalent to 100% of the duration of leave will be added on top, up to a maximum of 6 months additional allowance per period. Each case considered individually; supporting documents may be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: permanent posts and equivalent fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who hold a permanent post (including proleptic positions) in a UK university/NOT-FOR-PROFIT research organisation or have held an equivalent multi-year UK fellowship to establish an independent research group are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of ineligible previous fellowships include UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship, STFC Rutherford Fellowship, NERC Independent Research Fellowship, EPSRC Early Career Fellowship, Sir Henry Dale Fellowship, BBSRC David Phillips Fellowship. Postdoctoral training fellowships (e.g., Marie Skłodowska-Curie) are eligible; Dorothy Hodgkin Fellows may apply if they meet experience requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and visa eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants of all nationalities may apply; successful applicants requiring a visa to work in the UK are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa via a fast-track endorsement process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further visa guidance is on the Royal Society website. The Global Talent visa is designed for recognised leaders/potential leaders in their field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for disabled applicants and reasonable adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society welcomes applications from disabled scientists and will provide confidential support and adjustments to allow full participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments can include deadline extension, alternative formats (Word), additional interview support, accessibility software support, and reimbursement of additional costs to attend interviews. Requests are confidential and not normally shared with panel members unless relevant; permission will be sought if sharing is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host organisation type eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships must be held at eligible UK host organisations: UK Higher Education Institute (HEI), UK Research Council supported Research Institute (RCI), not-for-profit research institute (IRO), or Public Sector Research Establishment (PSRE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Royal Society webpage 'Organisations Eligible for Royal Society Research Funding' for full list. Candidates may remain at current institution but must explain route to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host commitments: Concordat and fair terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Host must confirm commitment to the Concordat for Research Careers and ensure research staff are appointed on terms no less favourable than comparable posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host must adopt principles/standards/good practice for management of research staff (training and development opportunities). Head of Department statement must confirm ability to comply with Conditions of Award and scheme-specific obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host commitments: diversity, inclusion and supportive environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Host Organisation must actively promote a supportive and inclusive research environment and ensure equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) is supported at all stages and activities of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Head of Department statement should describe current activities to create a supportive environment and transparent arrangements that led to applicant support. Panel members are briefed on unconscious bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host commitments: facilities, office/laboratory space and access to equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Host must provide necessary departmental and institutional support for the fellow, including adequate office/laboratory space and access to essential equipment, software and facilities from the start of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Head of Department should detail assurances and any additional support (funding, mentoring, training, networking) and clarify feasibility of requested staff (PDRA/PhD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Host commitments: protected fellowship time and permitted teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Host must ensure the award holder’s time is protected to concentrate on fellowship activities; Society funds 100% of fellow’s time but teaching/administrative duties should average no more than six hours per teaching week (pro‑rated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching includes student support, lecture/practical preparation and marking. Fellow determines spread of activities to best support research and career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion — scientific track record
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant’s scientific track record commensurate with research experience: past achievements, research career to date, publication record, likely contribution to the field, and potential to become a research leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track record is assessed relative to career stage and taking into account career breaks and pro‑rata time. Mid-fellowship also assesses updated track record since award start, including first/senior author publications where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion — scientific merit, originality, significance and likelihood of success
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality, originality and significance of the proposed research project and the likelihood of achieving goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels expect a clear five‑year project and a broader eight‑year vision/strategy; proposals should articulate contribution to the field and plans to disseminate outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion — clarity of plan and budget justification (5-year project and 8-year vision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and originality of the five-year project and an eight-year vision, plus a clear plan and justification for how the research budget will be used and how it will enhance the fellowship programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including funds for PhD students or PDRAs, outline training/support for these individuals. Budgets must be justified (salary spine point, relocation, research expenses, inflation, PhD stipend/fees). Failure to justify costs may lead to no award of funding for those items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion — suitability of host and research environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitability of the host organisation including appropriate expertise, equipment/resources, research environment and support for career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels expect host statements to confirm facilities, protected time, mentoring and additional support. Mid-fellowship review also assesses continued suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process and panel assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assessed by Research Appointment Panels (two Biological, three Physical), assigned by subject group/keywords; each proposal is initially reviewed by at least two panel members, with longlisting, independent peer review, reassessment, shortlisting and interview stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject tags selected by applicants are essential to assign panels and reviewers; interdisciplinary applications have a primary Review Panel and seconded members as needed. Timeline: eligibility checks → Panel Review 1 → longlist → independent peer review → Panel Review 2 → shortlist → interview → decision. Independent peer reviews may be shared with applicants upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition, confidentiality and unconscious bias briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel membership likely includes Fellows of the Royal Society and Members of the Royal Irish Academy; all reviewers are requested to consider applications in confidence and panels are briefed on unconscious bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Chairs provide oversight of longlisting/shortlisting; additional members may be seconded for interdisciplinarity. Applicants will be notified of outcomes by email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mid-fellowship review assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Mid-fellowship review assesses updated track record since start, evidence of independent research and building an independent career, proposed research project quality/originality and likelihood of achieving goals, and host institution suitability/support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding for years 6–8 of the fellowship is conditional on satisfactory mid-fellowship review at start of year four. Review is assessed by a member of the original Research Appointment Panel and ratified by Panel Chair. Decisions communicated within two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding cap and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request up to £1.87M total contribution from the Society over eight years; funding covers an 8‑year fellowship with costs for years 6–8 conditional on mid-fellowship review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cap is maximum Society contribution over 8 years. Applicants should include an assumed level of inflation for the full duration and justify the rate. The Society may award a salary different to that requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary contribution and justification (80% contribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society contributes 80% towards the Research Fellow’s basic salary and associated on‑costs; salary requested should be commensurate with skills, responsibilities and experience and not below the salary of equivalent early-stage academic posts in year 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary costs must be justified and supporting information may be requested at offer. Host organisations may top up salary at their discretion; the Society reserves the right to award a different salary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directly allocated and indirect costs and cost recovery rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Directly allocated (including estate) and indirect costs are funded at an 80% contribution rate; Other Directly Incurred Costs (consumables, equipment, travel) are 100% contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter values at appropriate FEC level (80% or 100%) in the budget table. Work with Host Organisation research/finance office when completing budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research expenses minimum expectation (£30,000 pa)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is expected that a minimum of £30,000 of research expenses per annum will be requested within the total award value of £1.87M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants in fields that typically require less may request less than the minimum but will need further justification to request the maximum grant value. There is no strict upper limit on research expenses per year provided the total does not exceed the cap; funds should be distributed as evenly as possible across fellowship years.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDRA funding: host contribution and feasibility evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting costs to support a PDRA, 80% of fEC salary costs may be requested and a statement from Head of Department is required confirming the host will cover 20% and clarifying feasibility of the appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include justification for staff costs and provide a supporting statement from the Host to confirm 20% cover and feasibility. Include spine point justification for any staff costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD studentship funding and transfer conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contribution to a 4‑year PhD studentship(s) (stipend and fees) can be requested at 100% contribution; PhD studentship length must be 4 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fellow transfers host or leaves, statements must confirm the PhD student can choose to stay or move with supervisor and that a deputy supervisor will be provided to take lead if fellow leaves. Provide full justification for PhD studentship requests and training offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement and training cost caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Research fellows may request up to £8,000 over the duration of the fellowship for public engagement and up to £8,000 for training/professional development (including training for staff/students supported on the award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These caps are cumulative over the 8-year fellowship and must be justified in the budget and application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment and large-cost justification (>£25,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any equipment costing more than £25,000 requires additional justification in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale and necessity for equipment purchases; include justification in the research expenses section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflation justification for full duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must include a reasonable assumed inflation level applied across budget headings for the full duration of the grant and justify the percentage used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no mandated min/max inflation rate but the Society reserves the right to reduce unreasonable rates. Exception: PhD studentships and fees excluded from inflation adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocation and visa expenses rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Relocation and visa costs can be included and the total grant cap may be exceeded to cover these costs if well justified; must include number of dependants, visa type and estimated costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relocation/visa costs for members of research group are not eligible. Justify these costs in the budget. Provide details of dependants (partner and children only).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget distribution and underspend carryover
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds should be distributed between fellowship years as evenly as possible; any underspend at end of a fellowship year can be carried over to the following year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input values in the budget table by fellowship year with year 1 = first year from 1 October 2026. Collaborate with Host research/finance office on entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory participants, references and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications require supporting statements/references from two individuals: the Head of Department (at Host) and one nominated Referee; both must submit via Flexi-Grant for the application to be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominated referee should be able to comment independently and authoritatively and must not be a named collaborator, a member of the assessment Panel, or a member of the Royal Society’s Council. Head of Department statement and referee must not be the same person. References must be in English; non-English references will not be accepted and may render the application ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Head of Department statement required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Head of Department must summarise candidate suitability and the Host Organisation’s commitments, including facilities, status/benefits parity, support (funding, mentoring, training), protection of fellowship time and feasibility of any requested PhD/PDRA appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Head of Department statement is visible to the applicant. Specific points to include are listed in the scheme notes (e.g., office/lab space, access to equipment, arrangements that led to support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants workflow and Flexi-Grant submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants (referees, Head of Department, Host Organisation approver) must have Flexi-Grant accounts and complete their contributions before the applicant can submit; the Host Organisation approver must approve by the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can invite participants via the 'participants' tab and monitor status (active/complete). If a participant submits prematurely, Lead Applicant can re-open that participant’s section. Recommended to get participant contributions at least 5 working days before deadline to allow approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system and deadline strictness
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted online via Flexi-Grant; paper applications will not be accepted. Late applications will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check eligibility and that all necessary information/evidence is presented prior to submission; applications without necessary information or evidence that assessment criteria are met will be rejected. Re-opening for participants is possible but institutional approval must be in place by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants should submit an ORCID identifier if they have one before their application is submitted; this is a mandatory requirement at the submission stage only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can register at orcid.org/register if they do not have one. Include ORCID to link outputs and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF/text upload formatting constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: PDF uploads: four sides of A4 only in portrait orientation; text smaller than Arial 10 should be avoided; add name and heading to top of every page; avoid security settings and colour/finely detailed illustrations; applications will be printed in black and white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If page length exceeded, text will be truncated. If using Text Field option, plain text only with maximum 2000 words; avoid symbols that may not be accepted by Flexi-Grant. Generate a PDF via 'print' to check appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support from named collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: If named collaborators are included, provide letters of support no more than one side of A4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should only provide information about collaborator’s role and confirm commitment to collaborate on the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management and data sharing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should deposit data outputs in appropriate, recognised, publicly available repositories and make data 'intelligently open' (discoverable, accessible, intelligible, assessable, reusable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Royal Society does not prescribe a fixed format for Data Management and Sharing Plans; applicants should focus on what data outputs will be generated, where/when they will be available, how others access data, limits on sharing for commercial/safety/privacy reasons, and long-term preservation strategies. Provide a plan if research will generate valuable data (max 200 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics approvals for animal and human research (Use of Animals / Human Participants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications involving animals must comply with the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986 and adopt 3Rs; applications involving human participants/tissue requiring local ethical approval must be accompanied by permission certificate or proof that ethical approval will be sought (in English).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should complete relevant questions on the Use of Animals/Human Participants pages if applicable. The Royal Society recommends using the NC3Rs Experimental Design Assistant (EDA) for animal experiments and uploading the EDA report if used (enter 'see report' or 'n/a' for duplicated fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant declaration and conditions of award acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must declare they have read the Terms and Conditions of Award and agree to abide by them if an offer is made, have access to necessary facilities for the project duration, and have agreed with Head(s) of Department that they will be afforded sufficient time and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms and Conditions are available on the Royal Society website; agreement is required at application submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generative AI disclosure and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Where generative AI tools are used in funding proposals, their use must be acknowledged by naming the AI source and specifying how the content was generated (e.g., listing the prompt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure AI use is responsible and complies with legal/ethical standards and Royal Society policies on Research Integrity and Trusted Research. Applicants are responsible for originality, validity, reliability, and integrity of any outputs created/modified by generative AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory diversity monitoring and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must complete mandatory diversity monitoring questions (or tick 'prefer not to say'); this information is kept separately and not seen by selection panel members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All questions are mandatory for system completion; the information forms a confidential statistical record under GDPR and is used only for analysis of Society activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness, eligibility checks and possible rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be checked for eligibility and completeness; non-submissions, ineligible, or incomplete applications will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility checks occur soon after round closes. At certain stages tailored feedback to unsuccessful applicants is not provided. Ensure all participants complete contributions and institutional approval is in place by the deadline to avoid rejection.
